title: streaming: lifecycle controls for client-cancel, disconnect/reconnect, and server timeouts (OpenAI compat)
author: Ivy Chen
description:
Context: several customers and e2e canaries observed flakiness when clients cancel or drop connections mid-stream. We also have mismatches with OpenAI streaming semantics around resume tokens and how 499-like client disconnects are surfaced by gateways. Motivation: reduce wasted GPU work on cancelled streams, ensure tool/function-calling events are not lost on reconnects, and make server timeout behavior observable and consistent with OpenAI compatibility expectations.

What this PR does:
- Adds lifecycle state machine hooks to the streaming connection manager to track client-cancel, disconnect, reconnect/resume and server-side idle/request timeouts.
- Implements resume-token generation and validation so clients that reconnect with a resume token can continue from the last acknowledged event (best-effort for function/tool calls and structured output).
- Changes server timeout handling to return a 499-style event in stream metadata when connection is closed by client and a 504-like error when request processing server-side times out. This aligns behavior with documented OpenAI compat patterns and improves observability in the Console.
- Preserves function/tool-calling events and structured output blocks across reconnect/resume where possible. When resume is impossible (KV cache invalidated or model state dropped), we fall back to a deterministic restart with a clear resume-failed marker in the stream.
- Adds comprehensive unit and e2e tests including flaky-connection scenarios and an OpenAI-compat smoke test.

Files changed (high-level): connection manager and handler logic, OpenAI compatibility adapter, streaming e2e tests, docs update.

Testing and CI: initial CI run surfaced nondeterministic e2e failures due to race in the connection cleanup path; race fixed with a single additional synchronization and CI passed on rerun. Performance microbenchmarks show a ~6% token-cost reduction for cancelled streams due to earlier cancellation propagation; latency for healthy streams unchanged within noise.

Backward compatibility and rollout: default behavior is opt-in via a feature flag (streaming.lifecycle_v2) enabled for a small percentage of traffic during rollout. OpenAI compatibility adapter is backward-compatible — clients without resume support will see the existing behavior.

Notes: this PR touches parts of the runtime and auth layers; security reviewed by Marisol. There are follow-ups planned to expose resume metrics in the Console and to extend resume semantics to multi-turn tool calls.
commits: feat(streaming): add lifecycle state machine for connections
fix(streaming): synchronize connection cleanup to avoid race on reconnect
feat(openai-compat): expose resume-token header and streaming metadata
docs(api): document streaming lifecycle and timeout semantics
review_comments: Raj Patel: Nice separation of state transitions — can you add a short comment explaining why we keep a soft TTL for resume tokens (vs absolute expiry)?
Ivy Chen: Added comment and a short test that verifies resume-token TTL semantics. Also made TTL configurable via feature flag.
Marisol Gomez: Security review: verified we don't leak internal model state in resume tokens and that tokens are HMAC'd with KMS key. Please include a note in changelog.
Ivy Chen: Added changelog entry and unit test asserting token HMAC verification fails with incorrect key.
Chris Liao: CI had a flaky e2e failure on first run (connection cleanup race). Re-ran and passed; please ensure we backport the sync fix to the 2024.11 patch branch.
Ivy Chen: Filed revert-safe backport PR to release/2024.11 (ENG-4901) and linked it above.
release_notes: Improves streaming stability on client cancels and reconnects: adds resume tokens, clearer timeout semantics (client disconnect vs server timeout), preserves function/tool call events across reconnects when possible. Opt-in rollout via streaming.lifecycle_v2 feature flag.
